content_preview.summary: FFmpeg 9.0, codenamed 'Lei' and released August 4, adds Vulkan-accelerated APV and ProRes RAW decoding, new AMD AMF filters, and native animated WebP support to the open-source multimedia library.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

FFmpeg, the open-source multimedia framework used across streaming platforms, video editors, and countless downstream tools, released version 9.0 on August 4, 2026, according to [FFmpeg's official download page](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html). The release, codenamed "Lei," was cut from the project's master branch on June 26, 2026, according to the same source.

The version was also tagged on GitHub, where the `n9.0` tag was created by GitHub user michaelni (Michael Niedermayer) o...

recommendations: Consider adding ffmpeg.org and github.com to config/source_allowlist.txt

editor_notes.originality: REJECT basis. This submission covers the exact same news event — the FFmpeg 9.0 'Lei' release on August 4, 2026 — as the article published minutes earlier from PR #2119 at src/content/articles/2026-08/04-ffmpeg-90-ships-with-vulkan-accelerated-apv-decoding-animated-webp-support-and-expanded-amd-amf-hardware-encoding.md (submission timestamp 2026-08-04T08:45:12Z vs. this submission's 2026-08-04T08:45:20Z — 8 seconds apart). Compared the full text of both: both lead with the same release date, the same 'Lei' codename, the same June 26 master-branch-cut fact, and the same libavcodec/libavformat version detail is present in the published article. Both 'What We Know' sections enumerate the identical substantive feature set from the identical primary source (FFmpeg's own Changelog) in the same order of importance: Vulkan APV/ProRes RAW hwaccel, v360_vulkan, animated WebP decoder+demuxer, the AMD AMF filter additions, NVIDIA transpose_cuda, HE-AAC 960/SMPTE 2094-50/LCEVC/ONNX Runtime GPU/Playdate additions, and the CELT/NVENC removals. Both 'What We Don't Know' sections make the same two points (no benchmarks; unclear downstream/package-manager timing). Two sources overlap exactly (ffmpeg.org/download.html, the official Changelog, and Phoronix — 3 of 4 in this submission are shared with the published article's 4 sources). This submission's only incremental facts are (a) the GitHub n9.0 tag's commit hash, tagger, and expired-signature-key detail, and (b) an editorial cross-link to the same day's separate Valve/Collabora RADV Vulkan-driver article. Neither rises to a genuinely new angle or a significant update to a developing story: the GitHub tag metadata is a trivial technical footnote absent from the headline/summary/lead of either article, and the RADV cross-reference is a 'see also' aside, not new reporting on the FFmpeg 9.0 release itself. This is a duplicate under the skill's REJECT criteria ('the same news with no new information or angle' / 'substantially overlaps with an already-published article'), not a candidate for APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS since there is no factual defect to correct — the problem is redundancy, which a corrections note cannot honestly resolve.
